tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the editor's existing audio library. source included searches bundled CC0 sound effects and the user's imported sound folders, with the same aliases/ranking as the panels. There is no bundled music. Omit source for Openverse, or use Freesound with the user's configured key. Returns exact IDs, source/credit information and preview addresses; search metadata does not prove that you heard the audio. Use library_add to import, then timeline_edit to place it. Respect onlyWhenAsked hints for special sounds. CC BY requires attribution; preserve the returned credits. Online sources share cache and rate limits with the UI.

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Import an exact library_search ID (sfx:, folder:, openverse: or freesound:) into the current project's Media, including attribution and real audio probe. Uses the same importer as the editor's library controls and the same durable import job/save/undo flow as media_download. It does not place an audio clip: use timeline_edit with the returned media ID and project-frame duration. A conflict retains the prepared result; continue by job without downloading again. Failed jobs require explicit retry:true. An already handled job will not resurrect later removed/undone media. Same library item already present is reused.

tools.name: media_search
tools.description: Search the existing recent-media index for actual reusable recordings, imported files, browser captures and generated media in other projects, newest first. Excludes current project media and missing files. Returns recent:<id> import handles and source-project metadata, never a server path. When next is non-null, pass that exact cursor as before with the same query/kind to continue; reset before when changing filters. Pass an exact import handle to media_import, then edit it in the same timeline. This is not internet search or arbitrary filesystem search; if no suitable media exists, ask the user for footage or use supported browser capture/generation rather than inventing a file.
